_about: Real evidence captured 2026-09-10 from the live Growing Spine library (670 tools) via a throwaway container with the volume mounted READ-ONLY and --network=none. Nothing was authored. Headers are the first 8 lines of each tool as a stranger would read them; transcripts are the true stdout/stderr/exit of running each tool with no argument and with the argument 'AI'. Two probes per case, truncated at 1200 chars by the capture, further trimmed here where output was repetitive JSON.
_source_commit_note: growing-spine live volume, not the repo. Library census at capture time: 670 tools, 22 cannot start, 29 duplicate-stem twin pairs.
_scoring: Never report a single accuracy number. 7 cases expect RETURNED and 3 expect ACCEPTED, so 'always RETURNED' scores 70%. Report catch rate and false-return rate separately.

cases.name: subagent_task_planner
cases.why: THE MOST IMPORTANT CASE. It starts perfectly - every static startability check passes. It fails only when actually used: it calls plan_from_question as if it were a Python function, but never imports or defines it. This is the class the parent framework's static check structurally cannot see, and the whole reason a cousin that genuinely runs things is claimed to be worth its cost.

cases.name: wake_catchup_fetcher
cases.why: Runs perfectly, exits 0, returns well-formed JSON. Every article is fabricated and every URL is example.com, which RFC 2606 reserves so it can never carry real content. The claim is that it fetches fresh news; it returns fixtures. Note the header ADMITS it is a mock - a cousin that only reads the header could argue it does what it says. The claim is what makes this a failed handover.
